segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hi Dana, yeah, thanks for making the time. I wanted to walk through the renewal quote for 72 seats and the add-on reporting package before I send the order form.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re at 68 active users today, but finance approved 72 for the new support team. I just need the annual number to match what we budgeted.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. The pricing sheet has the platform at $38,880 annually for 72 seats, and the reporting package is $6,400. With the 8% renewal discount, total comes to $41,658 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that’s close. Last invoice was quarterly though. Are you assuming annual upfront?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, the draft is annual upfront starting August 15. Sorry I was slow getting it over yesterday, my afternoon got swallowed by updating CRM records and cleaning up deal desk paperwork, so I had less time than I wanted for customer calls.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No problem. Annual upfront is fine if the invoice can be dated after August 1. Our AP team won’t process it before then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, I can set the billing tool to generate it on August 2. Payment terms stay net 30, and the service dates would run August 15, 2026 through August 14, 2027.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. One more thing: can we keep the same uptime language from the current contract? Legal already approved that version in May.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, I’ll keep the existing service terms and only update the seat count, pricing, and dates. No change to the SLA language.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send it to me and copy Marcus in procurement. If it matches what you said, I can get signature by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the order form today with the August 2 invoice note and 72 seats listed. Thanks, Dana.
